rows.subtopic: Stereotypes and how to challenge them
rows.subtype: Challenging a stereotype in a conversation [Response]
rows.description: A young adult hears a sweeping remark and asks a question or gives a personal example instead of attacking. People change more when their dignity is safe, and gentle challenge plants a real doubt.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: sadness, doubt, trust

rows.subtopic: Stereotypes and how to challenge them
rows.description: A young adult makes real friendships with people from groups they were warned about and tells the stories. Personal contact is one of the strongest cures for prejudice.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
possibly related concept (heuristic): Contact hypothesis (mixing groups reduces prejudice)

rows.description: A child of migrants speaks one language at home and another at school, and sometimes feels split. With warm support, the child grows into someone at ease in both worlds.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager born abroad to Indian parents feels foreign in both India and the new country. The search for identity is intense; friends with similar backgrounds and open family talk help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A parent abroad tightens rules on marriage, dress or language, fearing loss of the culture. It is love mixed with fear, and dialogue about what truly matters can soften rigid lines.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Not Indian enough or not local enough [Receiver]
rows.description: A young adult is told they are too Western at home and too foreign abroad. Hurtful labels show others' narrow ideas; the person can claim a blended identity without apology.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Returning to India after years abroad [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult back in India finds that home has changed and that they have too, and feels out of step. Patience with both the place and oneself brings a new fit over time.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult picks which customs, foods and values from each culture to hold as their own and passes them on with warmth. Identity becomes a garden tended by choice, not a cage.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young adult far from home builds a circle of friends who share a festival meal, a language or simply a kindness. Belonging can be built through shared time, not only shared ancestry.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A local sees a new arrival struggling with language and manners and offers a seat, an introduction or help with a form. Small welcomes make a place feel like home more than any speech.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
